subject: Customer ask: telemetry lockbox, derivative ownership & DPA carveouts
messages:
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@medialex.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions about telemetry, no-train commitments, and export controls

Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our legal and security teams as we evaluate a pilot:

1) No-training / model improvement opt-out — our legal wants a clear DPA carveout that confirms customer data (including prompts + responses) will not be used to improve models unless we opt in. Can you point us to the exact phrasing you support?

2) Telemetry & logs — we need an option where application telemetry (prompt logs, response snippets, telemetry traces) can be placed in a customer-controlled lockbox so that it isn't accessible to model-training pipelines. Is that available or would it require a Private deployment?

3) Subprocessor list & cross-border flow — please share the current subprocessor inventory and the default transfer path for EU-origin data (SFTP to EU residency or other).

I've attached a redline of your DPA for context (we shaded the clauses we want updated). We'll also want to discuss ownership of generated outputs — our IP counsel prefers an explicit "customer retains output IP" clause.

Can we set a call next week with your legal/ops folks?

Best,
Sara Jenkins
Head of Product Risk — MediaLex Analytics
Sara.Jenkins@medialex.com

Attachments: medialex-dpa-draft.docx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@medialex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions about telemetry, no-train commitments, and export controls

Sara —

Appreciate the clear notes and the marked-up DPA. Quick answers up front, then proposed next steps:

- No-train / model improvement: we support an explicit opt-out. Suggested clause text we've used with other enterprise customers: "Seller will not use Customer Content to improve Seller's models or training datasets without Customer's prior, written consent." We can include the language in the DPA and map an operational control (no-train flag) so traffic is excluded from improvement pipelines.

- Telemetry lockbox: two options depending on risk appetite:
  1) Hosted + Lockbox: we can route raw prompt/response logs into a customer-managed S3/GCS bucket or SFTP endpoint under your control (KMS-wrapped) and ensure logging pipelines don't feed model improvement. This is an ops configuration and does not require a Private control plane in many cases.
  2) Private / VPC deployment: full isolation; logs never leave your VPC and are under your KMS. This is available for customers with strict residency/air-gap needs.

- Subprocessors & transfers: we'll share the full subprocessor list and a data flow map. For EU-origin data we can route to EU residency pools or write to your EU SFTP; default hosted routing is region-aware but we will propose an explicit SFTP export path if you require it.

Next steps: can we schedule a 45-min call Monday (8/18) with Marissa (legal) and Dev (ops) to walk through a redline and operational controls? I've attached our SOC2 artifact and a high-level KMS diagram for the lockbox flow so your security team can review before the meeting.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: SOC2-report-Q2-2025.pdf, kms-architecture.png

From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@medialex.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions about telemetry, no-train commitments, and export controls

Thanks Jonas — that helps. A few clarifications from legal/security after reviewing your suggested language and the SOC2 snapshot: 

- The DPA needs an operational definition of "Customer Content" that explicitly includes prompts, responses, and attached user uploads. We also asked for a short "evidence" section that lists how Redwood will demonstrate compliance (e.g., audit log extract, attestation frequency).

- For the lockbox option (hosted + SFTP), we need assurances that the SFTP/S3 destination is KMS-wrapped with keys we control (customer-managed). Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept customer KMS keys, or will Redwood wrap with its KMS?

- Subprocessors: please mark which subprocessors have potential access to logs in plaintext vs. hashed/obfuscated forms. Our procurement team wants to know who could technically access data and whether any subprocessors are outside EEA/UK/US.

I've looped in Tom Park (security) to the thread — he'll join Monday's call. Attached is our redline with a suggested change to Section 3.2 (derivative rights) that starts from the wording you offered.

-Sara

Attachments: medialex-dpa-draft.docx (updated)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@medialex.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions about telemetry, no-train commitments, and export controls

Sara / Tom —

Thanks for the detailed markups. I read through the DPA redline and we can accommodate the asks with a combination of contract language and operational controls. Below are the proposed items we'll bring to the call and a short implementation note for each: 

1) Contract language (DPA):
- "Customer Content includes: (i) prompts and associated metadata; (ii) model responses; (iii) files and attachments uploaded by Customer users."
- "Seller will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve models that are used in Seller's public or commercial offerings without Customer's prior written consent."
- "Customer retains exclusive ownership of Generated Outputs unless otherwise agreed in writing."

2) Evidence & attestation:
- We can provide quarterly attestations and on-demand audit log extracts (redacted as needed). For higher-sensitivity customers we offer SOC2 + supplemental security assertions under NDA.

3) Lockbox & KMS:
- Hosted + Lockbox: we support writing telemetry to customer-owned S3 or SFTP endpoints. We can accept customer-managed KMS keys for the storage bucket (AWS KMS key policy permitting Redwood write access). Implementation requires a short runbook to set up a write-only service principal.
- Private: full KMS control in-customer VPC if you proceed with Private deployment.

4) Subprocessors & access levels:
- We'll provide a spreadsheet with subprocessors and a column for "level of access" (none / hashed / plaintext) and geography. Any subprocessor with plaintext access will be highlighted and we can propose mitigations (additional contractual obligations or technical isolation).

5) Operational plan & timeline:
- We typically implement hosted lockbox in 2-3 weeks once credentials/permissions are in place. Private deployments require a longer lead time (pricing + infra).

I'll bring a DPA redline with the language above to today's call and a short ops checklist for the hosted lockbox flow.

Proposed call: Mon 8/18 13:00 PT — Jonas, Dev, Tom, Sara? If that works I'll send a calendar invite and an agenda.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Ops — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Tom Park <tpark@medialex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@medialex.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions about telemetry, no-train commitments, and export controls

All —

Confirmed for 13:00 PT. On the KMS question: MediaLex prefers customer-managed keys for the lockbox. On the subprocessor spreadsheet please flag any 3rd parties located in APAC or LATAM — our compliance team will want to review.

Agenda request: please include a short ops demo of the hosted lockbox write flow (how logs are delivered and what redaction/obfuscation is available before write). Also want to see the audit log extract format so legal can validate the evidence ask.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Tom Park
Director, Security & Compliance — MediaLex Analytics
tpark@medialex.com
